title: If you get a filming notice or survey at your home or business

paragraphs: Info Page
What to do if you see a notice or survey posted on your building.

sections.heading: Filming notices
paragraphs: You may get a notice about filming in your neighborhood 72 hours before a shoot, if the production will:
Use 8 or more parking spots
Close lanes or streets
Film simulated violence or explosions
Film between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.
Have drone/UAS activity over moving vehicles or pedestrians

sections.heading: Filming notices › Access to your building
paragraphs: You will always have access to your private home during a shoot.
Traffic on your street may be stopped for safety reasons during filming. SFPD will be on-site if traffic needs to be stopped. Officers can help you get access to your home.

sections.heading: Filming notices › Contact the production’s location manager if you have questions about the production
paragraphs: The filming notice should contain their email or phone number. The location manager will be onsite during the shoot.

sections.heading: Filming notices › Contact Film SF if you have concerns about the shoot
paragraphs: Contact us at film@sfgov.org or 415-554-6241 to tell us your concerns about a current or future shoot in your neighborhood.
You can also contact us if you believe a film shoot is happening on your street and you didn’t get a notice about it.

sections.heading: Filming surveys
paragraphs: You may get a survey if a production plans on shooting on your street between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m if you are in a residential neighborhood. This survey is to get feedback from you, especially if you have concerns about the filming.
The survey will contain:
Details of the specific areas impacted
Hours of filming
Phone number and email address to collect your feedback

sections.heading: Filming surveys › Answering the survey
paragraphs: You do not have to provide your contact information.
If you live in an apartment building, your building manager may complete the survey for you.
